title: Caitlin Clark Volunteers For Fun Chicago Challenge During Offseason Appearance At MLB Stadium - NewsBreak
text:
By Kunal Pradeep Chawda ,
12 hours ago
The 2026 offseason would be over within the next 10 days, with the training camps and pre-season games leading to the actual season opener. Many players will return from vacations and other league games to rejoin their teams following the trades and free-agent signings. Caitlin Clark knows her destination, but still wants to be part of one off-court activity that came up recently.
While Angel Reese shone at the Victoria’s Secret campaign , CC is looking to visit Chicago for the contest announced by the city’s MLB team. The Cubs also welcomed her with open hearts.
Caitlin Clark (Image Credits: Imagn) Caitlin Clark Wants To Be Part Of Fun Chicago Challenge The Fever guard earlier showed support for the Chicago Cubs , which was a massive surprise for many fans, given her interest in Baseball. And now, before the start of the WNBA season, the 24-year-old wants to reunite with the team via a fun challenge.
The Chicago Cubs announced a recipe contest for chocolate chip cookies. The idea was to determine which participant has the best chocolate chip cookie recipe. The former Iowa star quickly took to social media and expressed her desire to be the art event’s special Tester as she wrote, “Would love to be the taste tester.”
The Cubs immediately responded with a resounding “ABSOLUTELY.” Interestingly, the whole contest is ‘online’: contestants submit their recipes and answer a few questions, but the winner gets a chance to serve the cookie at Wrigley Field.
Back to WNBA, the Indiana Fever made their first move, offering contracts to Kelsey Mitchell and Lexie Hull in the free agency. At the same time, the side lost two players in the WNBA Expansion Draft. The playmakers didn’t forget to show love for the outgoing stars.
Caitlin Clark Gives Farewell To Her Fever Teammates The WNBA started off the 2026 season with the expansion draft for the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo. While both teams selected 11 players each from 13 WNBA teams, the Fever side lost Chloe Bibby and Kristy Wallace in the draft.
Following their departures, both players shared emotional messages for the fanbase, teammates, and management, thanking them for their time at the franchise. The 2024 rookie responded to each of their messages, as on Bibby’s post, she wrote, “My Aussie for life.” The forward also returned love with a fun message, “Don’t cry too much.”
CC also responded to Wallace’s post with her nickname ‘Kdub ily’. The new Toronto Tempo player replied with a “big love mate” comment, showing close bonding amongst the Fever stars.
